titulo: A film without a video generator: photos and narration with 2.5D camera
lead: Not every film needs a video generator. Real photos or still images, a narration and one well-chosen camera move per photo already tell a story, with no credits spent and on any machine. The rehearsal clips in this course were made this way. Here you write the direction sheet and carry it out in an editor or with an agent.
objetivo: direct a film from photos and narration: one move, one duration and one transition per photo, without generating video.

aprende.t: Choose one camera move per photo based on what it shows
Measure each photo's duration by the narration
Use the hard cut as the default and save the calm shot for the end
Carry it out with keyframes in the editor or with the INEMA skills

hero_alt: A light table with printed photographs in layers, some cut out and mounted on supports of different heights, and a small camera slider pointed at them.

secoes.titulo: Photos and narration become a film
secoes.sub: Five decisions. Click on each one.

nos.detalhe: Your own photos, licensed archive photos or generated still images. A rich photo can become two or three shots (a wide, a detail). To move in close, use a large photo: at least 1920 px wide.
Record or synthesize the narration first (lesson 2). Each photo lasts as long as the part of the narration about it; never cut a sentence in the middle.

Moving in (push in) draws the viewer in; moving out (pull out) reveals the context; a tracking shot follows along; a static camera gives weight. A 2.5D camera separates foreground and background using the photo's estimated depth and moves one more than the other (parallax).
Hard cut as the default; dissolve for the passing of time; fade to black at the end. Never use the same transition on every photo.
No terminal: scale and position keyframes in the editor (2D movement, Ken Burns style). With a terminal: INEMA's pixflow and diretor-animacao skills do the 2.5D parallax and the look.

secoes.legenda: INEMA's diretor-animacao rules: never two identical movements next to each other, dramatic movement only once or twice in the film, and the last shot is the calmest.

secoes.titulo: How to direct the photos, step by step
secoes.sub: With the four images from the batch and a short narration.

texto: Write and record the narration before choosing the movements. Mark where each sentence starts: those marks are the photo durations.
If you can show it, don't narrate it: the photo of the dough makes the line "she kneads the dough" unnecessary. The narration says what the photo doesn't show.

exemplo.texto: "At 4:50 a.m., the street is still asleep." · "Dona Lia is already up." · "The first batch won't wait."

texto: A wide landscape calls for a slow push in or a tracking shot; a detail calls for a static camera or a short push in; a reveal calls for a pull out.

Don't repeat the same movement on neighboring photos, and save dramatic movement (dolly zoom, crash zoom) for once or twice in the film. A real photo gets parallax; drawings and illustrations get no parallax, only flat movement.
In the editor, place the photo on the timeline with the duration from your sheet and create two keyframes: scale and position at the start and at the end. The editor animates between them.
Concat has keyframes with curves. Use a smooth curve (ease) at the start and at the end so the movement doesn't jerk.

If you use Claude Code, you have INEMA's skills: diretor-animacao analyzes each image, proposes the shot list for you to approve, and renders through pixflow, which does the 2.5D parallax, 18 camera movements and ready-made looks.
They run on your computer with Node, FFmpeg and Chromium; without a dedicated graphics card, they render in software, more slowly. Neither of them uses video AI.

exercicios.titulo: Direction sheet · 4 to 12 photos, 30 to 60 s
exercicios.texto: Write the narration, mark the timing of each sentence, and fill in one line per photo with movement, duration and transition. Paste it into "Check your direction sheet" and download direcao-fotos.txt into the project folder.
exercicios.pronto: the page answers OK: [n] fotos com movimento, transição e tempo · [s] s, with the total between 30 and 60 s, and the file is in the project folder.

exercicios.titulo: Render · the sheet becomes a video
exercicios.texto: Run the sheet in the editor with keyframes (or with the diretor-animacao skill, if you use a terminal), with the narration underneath, and export as MP4 H.264. Check the file in the "Check your short film" section of lesson 8, which accepts the same 30 to 60 s as the sheet.
exercicios.pronto: the "Check your short film" section of lesson 8 answers OK: [s] s · [w]×[h] · [p] for the file.

secoes.sub: Four questions. The explanation appears after each answer.

perguntas.p: What decides how long each photo stays on screen?
opcoes: The photo's file size: a bigger photo stays longer.
One fixed value for all of them, which keeps the pace even.
The chosen movement: an orbit lasts longer than a static camera.
The part of the narration that talks about that photo.
perguntas.explica: The narration sets the timing: each photo lasts as long as its part of the speech, without cutting the sentence. A fixed time for all of them makes the film mechanical.

perguntas.p: What is the difference between the editor's 2D movement and the 2.5D camera?
opcoes: In 2.5D, foreground and background move at different speeds (parallax).
2D only works on vertical photos and 2.5D only on horizontal ones.
2.5D needs a paid video generator and a dedicated graphics card to work.
There is no difference: they are two names for the same effect.
perguntas.explica: In 2D the whole photo moves together (scale and position). In 2.5D the foreground moves more than the background (parallax), with no video AI.

perguntas.p: Your sheet has push in, push in and orbit in a row. What does diretor-animacao recommend?
opcoes: Keep it: repeating the movement gives the photo sequence unity.
Swap the three transitions for long dissolves, to smooth the sequence.
Swap one of the push ins: never two identical movements in neighboring photos.
Speed up all three movements so they fit in less time.
perguntas.explica: A movement repeated in neighboring photos makes the film mechanical. Swap one of them for another movement or for a static camera.

perguntas.p: Which transition should the sheet use as the default?
opcoes: Dissolve on all of them, so the film feels smooth.
Hard cut, saving dissolve and fade for when they tell something.
Whip pan on all of them, to give a social media rhythm.
Fade to black between each photo, to separate the ideas.
perguntas.explica: A hard cut is the most invisible. A dissolve marks the passage of time and a fade to black marks an ending; used on every photo, they lose their meaning.

itens.texto: Each photo lasts as long as its part of the speech.
Chosen by what the photo shows; the last shot is the calmest.
Keyframes in the editor, no terminal; pixflow and diretor-animacao, with a terminal. Neither spends credits.
